title: Resource tenancy lattice and guarded role mapping for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and validate a production-ready RBAC v2 role model that maps roles to a multi-dimensional resource tenancy lattice and provides deterministic permission reconciliation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This ticket captures the design for role projection, scope resolution, permission matrix encoding, audit logging hooks, and SSO group/SCIM mapping considerations. It also includes a migration and rollout strategy that minimizes blast radius for existing customers.
background: Current RBAC (v1) mixes tenant-level admin flags and ad-hoc role grants. That model has produced ambiguous behavior when a user has grants at multiple resource levels (org, project, pool) and during transitions to Dedicated or Private deployments where isolation boundaries are stricter. RBAC v2 aims to be explicit about resource tenancy dimensions, support hierarchical and lattice-like scope composition, and provide a single reconciliation algorithm so decisions are auditable and testable.
proposal_summary: Introduce a tenancy lattice model (dimensions: Org, Project, Pool, Model, Environment) where a scope is a coordinate in that lattice. Roles are canonical sets of permissions expressed as action:resource templates (for example 'deploy:pool' or 'read:model'). Role bindings include an explicit scope coordinate and an optional inheritance policy (none | children | explicit). Permission reconciliation uses precedence rules: explicit deny > role grants at exact scope > inherited grants from nearest ancestor scope > global grants. Ties are resolved deterministically by scope distance then by role priority. Audit events are emitted on grant/eval with full decision context.
resource_hierarchy: Project - logical grouping of resources belonging to an org
Pool - Dedicated or shared GPU pool; used for capacity and isolation
Model - model artifact serving instance or catalog entry
scope_concepts: Scope coordinate: JSON path-like identifier (org:acme,project:billing,pool:dedicated-east) - represented as flat string for storage
Scope composition: ability to express wildcards and partial coordinates (project:* or pool:dedicated-*)
Scope inheritance: explicit policy determines whether child resources inherit parent role bindings
Scope distance: computed number of differing coord components used in precedence decisions
permission_matrix_examples: Role: BillingViewer => permissions: read:billing-usage, read:billing-invoices scoped to project or org
Role: PoolOperator => permissions: deploy:pool, scale:pool, drain:pool scoped to pool or above if inheritance enabled
Role: ModelReader => permissions: read:model, embed:create scoped to model, project
Implicit deny example: deny:delete:model can be attached at org-level for compliance and will override lower-level allow
permission_reconciliation_algorithm: 1) Gather all role bindings applicable to the request actor and resource coordinate. 2) Filter by explicit denies; if any deny matches action+resource pattern => deny. 3) Evaluate exact-scope allows. 4) Evaluate inherited allows ordered by increasing scope distance (nearest ancestor first). 5) If multiple allows from same distance, choose allow from highest role priority. 6) Default deny.
audit_logging_integration: Emit immutable 'permission_evaluation' events for every decision containing: actor_id, effective_role_ids, matched_bindings (list of binding ids), decision (allow|deny), timestamp, scope_coordinate, resource_snapshot (resource id, type), and evaluation_trace (list of rule applications). Logs stored in append-only store (WORM) with retention configurable per customer; console will surface recent evaluations and sample traces. Grant/revoke operations also emit 'role_binding_change' events with actor, target_binding, before/after metadata and request id for correlation.
sso_scim_mapping_and_scopes: SSO group mapping will be first-class: group->role_binding connector which can be push-provisioned via SCIM or evaluated at runtime via SAML group assertions. Mapping rules support conditions (e.g., only provision group->role if subject email domain matches) and support mapping to scope-scoped bindings (e.g., 'acme-admins' -> role:OrgAdmin at org:acme). SCIM sync must support delta updates and graceful handling of missing principals.
admin_controls_and_breakglass: Provide a delegated-admin model where admins can be granted limited admin roles scoped to specific orgs/projects. Add a 'breakglass' emergency role that requires justification and is timeboxed; breakglass grants are logged to audit with high alert priority. Admin actions that modify other admin bindings must require an additional approval step (configurable by org). Support 'role review' workbench in Console for periodic attestation and bulk expiration of stale bindings.
migration_plan: Phase 0: Telemetry - run RBAC v2 simulator in read-only mode against historical events to identify conflicts and ambiguous binds
Phase 1: Convert - automatic conversion script that projects v1 flags to closest v2 roles using heuristics; create 'converted' bindings tagged for review
Phase 2: Parallel eval - enable dual-eval where both v1 and v2 are evaluated; comparisons emitted to a 'reconciliation' dashboard
Phase 3: Canary - roll out v2 enforcement to selected internal orgs and a small set of external beta customers
Phase 4: Enforce - flip enforcement flag org-by-org after attestation and monitoring window
rollout_and_backout: Canary group for internal infra and non-critical customers for 2 weeks, monitor for false denies.
Backout plan: revert flag for org, run automatic restoration of previous role bindings, emit rollback incident notes
Escalation path: SRE on-call + security lead + PM for any customer-facing denial regressions
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic reconciliation algorithm implemented and unit-tested with >95% path coverage
Audit events contain required fields and are queryable by request id and actor id within the Console
SCIM provisioning connector can create/update/delete group bindings and a sample SAML provider can map groups to scoped role_bindings
Migration converter produces a report with mappings and an actionable list of manual reviews (<5% of total bindings)
Canary customers experience no regression in permissions for critical flows after 2 weeks
testing_plan: Property-based tests for scope distance and precedence decisions
Integration test harness that simulates multi-tenant membership and validates audit traces
Chaos tests: random grant churn during evaluation window to validate idempotency and audit ordering
Performance test: permission evaluation tail latency must be <2ms p95 for common case (cached bindings)
open_risks: Risk: Large orgs with thousands of group binds may see higher storage and evaluation cost. Mitigation: incremental caching and snapshotting of effective bindings per actor with TTL.
Risk: SCIM delta races could produce transient missing bindings; mitigate via eventual consistency and retry semantics with idempotency keys.
Risk: Determinism across replicas requires strict ordering guarantees on binding updates; mitigate by using vector timestamps and monotonic commit sequence numbers
